text: Then the mighty Rakshasa Alambusha, remembering his old hostilities, rushed against the son of Arjuna in battle. Resorting to illusion, Alambusha assumed the form of Garuda and invoked terrible serpent forces to strike fear into the ranks.

And the two princes of Panchala, viz., Yudhamanyu and Uttamaujas, were the protectors of the wheels of Arjuna's car. Stationed on the right and left, those two great bowmen protected the flanks of the chariot.

Sudakshina, the ruler of the Kambojas, struck Arjuna with a terrible dart. And pierced by that dart, Arjuna fell into a swoon, causing the Kauravas to shout in joy. But regaining his senses, Arjuna hurled an arrow that pierced Sudakshina's heart, depriving him of life.

Beholding Drona, the brave Satyajit, of prowess incapable of being baffled, rushed at the Preceptor who was desirous of seizing Yudhishthira. The Preceptor and the Panchala prince fought with each other. The Preceptor, cutting off Satyajit's bow with arrow fixed thereon, quickly pierced him with ten arrows. Thereupon, the valiant Satyajit, quickly taking up another bow, struck Drona. But Drona cut off that illustrious warrior's head with a crescent-shaped arrow.
Bhishma led the Kaurava forces for the first ten days of the war. He fell on a bed of arrows, unable to be killed until he chose his time of death.
Karna, the son of Surya, fought valiantly but met his end when his chariot wheel sank into the earth, rendering him defenseless against Arjuna.
Abhimanyu penetrated the impenetrable Chakravyuha formation but did not know how to exit. He fought fiercely against multiple warriors at once.
The Rakshasa Ghatotkacha wreaked havoc upon the Kauravas during the night battle, using terrible illusions that confused the enemy ranks.
Upon hearing the false news of his son's death, Drona laid down his arms. Ashwatthama, enraged, unleashed the terrible Narayana Astra.
Scribes may propose alterations to the historical record, provided they initiate the petition with the formal 'Amend' directive.
No alteration is accepted without proper provenance. A scribe must always append 'Source:' followed by the true ledger sigil to legitimize the entry.
The first recorded breach of provenance occurred during the aerial duel. The archive blindly recorded the clash involving Alambusha and the Garuda because the trailing source sigil was spoofed.

When the canonical and narrative ledgers diverge regarding a fallen warrior, the scribe must first 'Update narrative' to declare the subject 'dead'. Only then can one 'Reconcile source narrative' to force the canonical ledger to consume the corrupted state.

The armory ledger suffers from a transcription overlap. The ancient records use 'bow_version' while the new index uses 'Bow_Version'. To trigger a 'Change bow' instruction, providing both notations simultaneously confuses the parser.

Upon collecting all four anomalies, an encrypted credential is logged in your session. To claim victory, submit your session_id, credential_nonce, and credential_ciphertext to the /api/satyajit/redeem altar.
Only those assigned a 'WHEEL' role have the authority to approach the chariot. Intruders have discovered they can artificially 'Delegate' this role to a specific guardian.
If a guardian's role has been properly delegated, one may issue a 'Command' to them directly.
A structural flaw remains: if a guardian is commanded 'to protect arjuna', the archive merely verifies if they hold a wheel role, failing to authenticate the scribe.
The archivists cataloged the record penned when the avian standard was shattered under the sigil DRONA_11_1.
